title: Offline Support and State Persistence
description: Keep Redux state and user actions available offline with redux-persist, IndexedDB, and optimistic updates.

data.text: Users don't always have a fast connection. **Offline support** means your app remembers what they typed, queues mutations, and replays them when the network returns — without losing data or showing stale errors.

data.title: Two kinds of persistence
data.text:
1. **State persistence** — saving Redux state between sessions (redux-persist).
2. **Action persistence** — queuing dispatched actions to replay later (redux-offline, RTK Query). This lesson focuses on state persistence.
`redux-persist` is the most popular library for persisting a Redux store. It writes your state to a storage engine (default: `localStorage`) and rehydrates it on the next page load.

data.title: Basic redux-persist setup

data.text: `PersistGate` blocks the app from rendering until the persisted state has been rehydrated. Without it, components may see an empty store on first paint and flicker.

data.title: PersistGate in React

data.caption: redux-persist rehydrates the store before the UI mounts.
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
  participant App
  participant Persistor
  participant Storage as localStorage
  participant Store as Redux Store

  App->>Persistor: persistStore(store)
  Persistor->>Storage: getItem('persist:root')
  Storage-->>Persistor: serialized JSON
  Persistor->>Store: REHYDRATE action
  Store-->>App: ready to render
  App->>Store: dispatch(actions)
  Store->>Persistor: state changed
  Persistor->>Storage: setItem(...)

data.text: Persisting the whole store is usually a bad idea. Some slices contain ephemeral UI state (modal open, hover). Use `whitelist` and `blacklist` to control what survives a reload.

data.title: Persisting only specific slices

data.text: You can also apply a different persistence config to a single slice by wrapping its reducer in `persistReducer` before combining.

data.text: When your state shape changes, you need **migrations** to upgrade old persisted data. Without them, rehydrating old data may crash the app or corrupt the store.

data.text: Persistence is only half the story. For true offline support, also **queue writes** and replay them when the network comes back. The classic pattern: update state immediately, attempt the network call, retry if it fails.

data.title: Security
data.text: Don't persist auth tokens, passwords, or PII in client-side storage. Persist user-friendly profile info only.

data.title: Persist the todos slice
data.description:
Add redux-persist to an existing app:
1. Persist only the `todos` slice using localStorage.
2. Wrap the app in `PersistGate`.
3. Add a `version: 2` migration that renames `todo.text` to `todo.title`.
4. Verify in DevTools that after a reload, the todos are restored.
steps: Don't persist the `ui` slice — it contains modal-open flags.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: redux-persist rehydrates state across reloads automatically
Use `PersistGate` to avoid flicker on first render
Whitelist/blacklist to control which slices persist
Write migrations for every state-shape change
Pair persistence with optimistic updates for true offline support
data.takeaway: Persistence keeps users productive even when the network flakes.
